items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: the popular R&B groups were like Rick James or Parliment Funkadellic, Kool and the Gang. So we were into listening to that at the time

ctx.x: He was an organist, but he mainly played piano. Mainly played piano. And I remember him trying to get us to take piano at an early age. And it was really hard to sit at the piano for one-two-three, doing exercises and right outside of the window you could hear loud and clear the boys playing football and shooting marbles. It was like oh I don’t want to do this. And he didn’t make us do it, but we were offered to have music lessons because he also taught. But I took piano later on, I think when I was eleven I…

everything from slave chants up into modern jazz and what they called modern jazz at that time, was up to the Dizzy Gillespie Big Band. And there was “Sonnymoon for Two” by Sonny Rollins, but of everything that I listened to I really loved the side that had the New Orleans jazz on it. I mean it had ragtime, it just had ten different idioms of jazz if you would. And I listened to the “Keyhole Blues,” by Louis Armstrong, and I was in my second, going into my third year playing trombone maybe. And so I began to try…
